articleTitle: Flexible Grounding Line Selection Based on Power Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Aiming at the difficulty of flexible grounding line selection, a fault line selection method based on the phase change characteristics of zero sequence power is proposed. Based on the equivalent circuit of single-phase grounding fault in flexible grounding system, the difference characteristics of zero-sequence active power between intact line and fault line before and after neutral point parallel connection with small resistance are analyzed. It is found that there are significant differences between the waveforms of low-frequency reactive components of intact lines and faulty lines. The difference of steady-state zero-sequence active power between lines is compared by Hausdorff distance algorithm, and the implementation scheme of fault line selection is designed through the fault line selection criterion of Hausdorff distance parameters. The correctness and effectiveness of the proposed line selection scheme are verified by the calculation and analysis of Matlab simulation and experimental waveform records.

articleTitle: Multi-Time Scale Voltage Distribution Characteristics Analysis of Distribution Transformers Based on Data Mining Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: With the construction of new power systems, the randomness and uncertainty of distribution voltage are increased by the large number of nonlinear loads and distributed photovoltaics. The development of intelligent distribution network enables power grid enterprises to obtain massive voltage data of distribution transformers. Based on data mining technology, this paper analyzes the voltage distribution characteristics of regional distribution transformers, explores the clustering method of regional distribution transformer, and realizes voltage early warning by combining the prediction results, so as to improve the precision level of voltage management.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Integrated Electricity-Hydrogen-Heat Energy System Considering Long-Term Low-Output Events of Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The long-term low-output events (LLEs) of wind power are usually difficult to capture. The previous modeling methods often disassemble such events, resulting in the loss of key information. In view of this problem, a new 3D index modeling method is proposed in this paper. Then, an empirical mode decomposition-priority chronological time-period clustering (EMD-PCTPC) algorithm is developed. This method can not only effectively retain the chronological order of the original wind power output, but also fully retain the LLEs in a long time scale. On this basis, an optimal planning model of integrated electricity-hydrogen-heat energy system is built. Through the verification of the IEEE-33 node power system and the 6-node thermal system, the results show that the EMD-PCTPC algorithm successfully reduces the total cost by 4.31%, and significantly reducing the loss of load by 57.4%, which promotes the stable operation of the integrated energy system.

articleTitle: An Analysis Method for Recognizing and Analyzing Multi-type Documents in Electric Power Operation Site Based on PaddleOCR
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The power operation site produces a large number of documents of various types and complex structures every day, and manual review of these documents is very time-consuming. In order to improve the review efficiency, a multi-type document recognition and analysis method based on PaddleOCR is proposed for the power operation site. First, the input documents are preprocessed, including format conversion and image correction. Then, the region of interest is obtained by PaddleOCR and classified into tabular and non-tabular types, which are recognized and analyzed using the tabular detection recognition model and traditional image processing methods, respectively. In particular, a multi-page document splicing method with text position adjustment by calculating page number information and average line spacing and a signature body recognition scheme based on feature extraction network and cosine similarity calculation are proposed to solve the challenges of multi-page document recognition and signature recognition. The experimental results verify the effectiveness of the method under different conditions, which significantly improves the efficiency of reviewing power operation documents.

articleTitle: Study on Two-phase Optimized Scheduling of Virtual Power Plant Based on Scheduling External Encapsulation Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In order to solve the increasingly serious problem of insufficient power resources, virtual power plants have become a research hotspot in recent years. At present, there is a lack of research related to the aggregation of scheduling characteristic parameters of virtual power plants in China, and virtual power plants often appear to be of different sizes, resulting in large discrete scheduling data and unstable scheduling processes. This paper proposes a two-phase optimal scheduling model for virtual power plants based on scheduling external encapsulation standards. In the first phase, the grid dispatch center proposes the scheduling external encapsulation standard and screens out the virtual power plants that meet the standard to participate in the actual scheduling; in the second phase, the agents of the virtual power plants carry out the assignment of power generation tasks among the internal power generation units. This method ensures that the virtual power plants' scheduling characteristic parameters meet the dispatch center's requirements and habits. Arithmetic simulation analysis using the improved IEEE14 node model. The results show that the model can effectively shorten the total scheduling time and increase the stability of the scheduling process at the same time.

articleTitle: Solar Photovoltaic Lighting for Community Service Improvement and Sustainable Renovation Design and Application Case in Chengdu, China
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: China is currently at the peak of urban construction, and the rapid development of urban infrastructure has led to the swift growth of street lighting. The resulting energy consumption has become an indispensable factor affecting people's daily lives. Urban road lighting is a crucial part of road planning and design, especially in this era of intense urbanization. In the context of energy constraints, lighting consumes a substantial proportion of energy, and the total amount of energy used for lighting each year is significant. This study takes Caojia Lane Workers' Village in Jinniu District, Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, as an example and proposes a landscape lighting pattern of “three rings and one axis”, considering the current situation of Caojia Lane Workers' Village. PVsyst and other software were used to obtain relevant meteorological data, select two extreme days for analysis, simulate and analyze the installation angle and area of the solar photovoltaic system, and calculate the thermal economy of solar PV lighting to explore the feasibility of applying solar PV systems in street lighting in this community. Preliminary results indicate that the application of this solar PV system to street lighting in Caojia Lane Workers' Village has significant economic benefits.

articleTitle: Research on Internal Short-circuit Fault Diagnosis Based on Correlation Coefficient Method
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Battery energy storage systems are typically composed of lithium-ion battery packs. Among many battery faults, internal short-circuit faults pose the most serious hazards, and diagnosing and locating such faults has attracted widespread attention. This paper focuses on battery modules and adopts an improved correlation coefficient method. By reducing computational complexity through a sliding time window, it compares the correlation coefficients of battery voltages collected by adjacent sensors. Based on the steep drop characteristics of correlation coefficients caused by the consistency difference between faulty battery voltages and normal battery voltages, this paper diagnoses and locates internal short-circuit faults within battery packs. Experimental results show that this method can effectively locate and diagnose faulty batteries based on correlation coefficient threshold judgments.

articleTitle: A Fast Diagnosis Method for Internal Short Circuit Fault in Energy Storage Batteries Based on Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Internal short circuits are common extreme battery faults. Due to the unclear characteristics of external voltage changes, early diagnosis of internal short circuit faults has received widespread attention. To address the issue of early warning, this paper proposes a fast diagnostic method for internal short circuit faults in batteries based on electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). Firstly, by applying pulse current excitation to the battery, the voltage response results of the battery are collected, combined with wavelet transform to obtain the EIS of the battery in multiple frequency bands. Based on this, Nyquist plots are drawn to compare batteries with different simulated short-circuit levels, and the trend of curve changes are observed. Then, a battery internal short circuit fault diagnosis experimental testing platform was built to verify this method. The results showed that the fast calculation method based on pulse current excitation and response can accurately obtain AC impedance of 0.1Hz-10Hz, with a root mean square error of 0.44m Ω in the real part and 0.22m Ω in the imaginary part. The fast acquisition method of battery impedance spectrum can effectively diagnose internal short circuit. Diagnose internal short circuit faults and their severity based on the slope of the Nyquist plot line and the offset of the intersection point between the line and the semi-circular part. This method can be used for daily fault diagnosis, which is beneficial for ensuring the safety of residential battery use.

articleTitle: An Efficient Data Transmission Protection Method for IoT Terminals Based on Temporary Ciphertext Stream Resource Pool
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Industrial IoT terminals are sensitive to device costs, which limits the application of high-performance encryption modules with PCIE and USB interfaces. Currently, security chips (or modules) are generally used to encrypt data, and this method has a long processing delay for large amounts of data. The present invention optimizes data encryption and decryption, integrity protection strategies and processes by constructing a temporary ciphertext data stream resource pool to meet the needs of high real-time and high bandwidth data secure transmission in industrial Internet of Things application scenarios. Experience has shown that this solution significantly improves data encryption and decryption efficiency while ensuring economic and business security.

articleTitle: Coordinated Planning of Integrated Electricity and Hydrogen Microgrids Considering Hydrogen Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Long-term energy storage plays a key role in power systems, especially in dealing with the volatility of renewable energy generation. How to coordinate the energy continuity of long-term energy storage between typical days has become a crucial research direction. Recognizing the critical role of long-term energy storage in trans-seasonal energy regulation, this paper proposes an operation model for hydrogen storage that ensures continuous energy flow between typical days. The model comprehensively considers the energy interconnection and balance requirements across multiple time scales to maintain the stable operation of the energy storage system. Additionally, it incorporates the fast response capabilities of short-term energy storage to guarantee the smooth and efficient functioning of the power system both within individual days and across typical days. This optimization of energy interconnection not only improves energy utilization efficiency but also strengthens the system's ability to coordinate scheduling across various time scales, significantly increasing the integration of renewable energy and ensuring long-term system stability

articleTitle: Remotely Accessible Cyber-Physical System Testbed for Power Grid's Security and Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity and integration of digital technologies in power grids, ensuring their security and reliability has become a critical challenge. Cyber-physical threats pose significant risks to the stability and functionality of these systems. To address these challenges, there is a need for comprehensive testbeds that can simulate real-world scenarios and assess the resilience of power grid operations under various cyber-physical attack vectors. This paper presents a remotely accessible cyber-physical system (CPS) testbed that we designed and built to study the security and reliability issues of power grids. Utilizing Node-RED in the front-end and integrating GridPACK, HELICS, and NS3 in the back-end, the testbed provides comprehensive capabilities for simulating, monitoring, and analyzing power grid performance under various scenarios, including various kinds of cyber-attack. The CPS testbed enables us to measure performance metrics such as network latency, packet loss, voltage stability, and system response time are monitored under normal and attack conditions through various simulations and real-time data analysis. This testbed provides a valuable tool for researchers and engineers to study and improve power grid security and resilience.

articleTitle: Study on the Impact of SVG Active Harmonic Elimination on Inverter Side of LCC
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The SVG is a commonly used reactive power compensation device in LCC converter stations to enhance the system's ability to withstand commutation failures. Although the SVG has advantages such as fast response and minimal impact from bus voltage drops, the harmonics generated by the SVG itself can affect the effectiveness of the converter transformer's filtering of the 5th and 7th harmonics. This paper analyzes the principle that the converter transformer's filtering of the 5th and 7th harmonics, and then take the impact of SVG on grid-side harmonics when performing functions such as reactive power compensation or characteristic subharmonic filtering into account, and finally, builds a simulation model in SIMULINK to verify the accuracy of the analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Lightning Protection Performance and Parameter Selection of Lightning Protection Insulator for ±500kV DC Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The lightning fault of the ± 500kV DC transmission line constitutes a significant proportion, and the situation regarding lightning protection is severe. Currently, there is limited research on the lightning characteristics of ± 500kV DC transmission lines after installing arresters or lightning protection insulators, as well as their performance with different parameters. This study takes the ± 500kV Jiangcheng DC transmission line as an example to calculate the maximum shielding failure current using the electrical geometry method. An electromagnetic transient simulation model of the transmission line is established to analyze and calculate the action characteristics of lightning protection insulators under shielding failure conditions. Additionally, this study calculates and analyzes the influence of ground inclination angle and parameter selection for lightning protection insulators on their shielding failure performance. The findings presented in this paper can serve as a reference for selecting appropriate parameters for lightning protection insulators.

articleTitle: A Method for Small Current Grounding Fault Location Based on the Modified D-S Evidence Theory with Multi-Criteria Basic Belief Assignment Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In order to overcome the limitations and insufficient accuracy of the single identification method of small current grounding fault and enhance the applicability of the identification method, a method for small current grounding fault location based on the modified d-s evidence theory with multi-criteria basic belief assignment adjustment is proposed. Firstly, the duality and difference of fault characteristics of zero-sequence current and phase current after single-phase grounding fault are analyzed. Based on the three methods of transient zero-sequence reactive power direction, zero-sequence capacitance parameter identification and phase current mutation direction, the fault characteristics are binarized to construct the fusion sub-criterion. Then, the performance of each criterion is evaluated by using the historical discriminant confusion matrix and the check reliability factor of the two nearest neighbor discriminants. According to the positive judgment rate of each criterion, the basic belief assignment is dynamically modified in a data-driven manner to ensure that the high-accuracy criterion obtains higher basic belief assignment. Based on the D-S evidence theory, the multi-criteria information is fused to form a comprehensive criterion for small current grounding fault. Finally, the simulation model is constructed in DigSilent/PowerFactory, and the simulation waveforms under 1000 random fault scenarios are tested. The results show that the correct rate of the proposed method is 90.6 %, and it has a high correct rate in different fault scenarios, which is better than a single criterion, which verifies the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Multi-terminal Differential Protection Based on Composite Criterion for T-connected Distribution Network with Inverter Interfaced Distributed Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The access of inverter interfaced distributed generator (IIDG) challenges the protection configuration of traditional distribution network. In this paper, a composite criterion of multi-terminal differential protection for T-connected distribution networks is proposed. Firstly, the impact of IIDG on relay protection of distribution network is analyzed, and the problems of two differential protection criteria with IIDG integration are studied. Then, based on the control strategy and output characteristics of IIDG, a multi-terminal current differential protection with composite criterion applicable to IIDG accessing distribution network is proposed. Finally, the T-connected distribution network model of IIDG is constructed in the simulation software, and the action characteristics of the newly proposed multi-terminal differential protection based on composite criterion is simulated and analyzed under different fault types and fault locations.

articleTitle: Early Warning Method for Overload of Massive Transformer Based on TL-LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: To address the issues of low prediction accuracy and limited capability in handling large datasets in power load forecasting methods, this paper proposes a novel load forecasting model based on transfer learning (TL) and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks. Firstly, using the maximum mutual information coefficient method (MIC) to select high relevance load features; Secondly, a load prediction model is constructed by employing transfer learning and long short-term memory networks to effectively predict the loads of a large number of substations; Finally, using the predicted load rate and the heavy overload assessment criteria, the final heavy overload warning results for distribution substations are determined. Compared with the traditional method, this method can greatly improve the model's ability to handle big data and retain the timeliness of load forecasting while maintaining a certain level of forecasting accuracy.

articleTitle: Design of Front-End Power Supply for Lithium Battery Equalization Charging System
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In order to meet the front-end power supply requirements of the lithium battery equalization charging system, this paper designs a flyback DC-DC converter based on the UCC28740 chip, analyzes and calculates the main parameters of the circuit topology. Meantime, this paper also establish a small signal model of which feedback control, and base on that, this paper design a feedback control network which composed of TL431 and optocoupler to improve the stability and reliability of the system. At last, the results of the experiment verifies that the output power supply is stable, its response speed is fast, and the robustness is good.

articleTitle: User Cost Differences under Five Capacity Adequacy Mechanisms Based on Equilibrium Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Capacity adequacy mechanisms are crucial pathways to ensure reliable power supply in electricity grids and are coupled with the spot electricity market. However, current studies on the impact of capacity adequacy mechanisms on the electricity market do not simultaneously consider the strategies of power generators regarding bidding, investment, and capacity sales, as well as the strategic behaviors among multiple stakeholders. To address this, we propose game-theoretic equilibrium models for multiple power generators under five typical capacity adequacy mechanisms: scarcity pricing, strategic reserve, capacity subsidy, capacity market, and reliability options. Firstly, we establish a two-layer game model for each capacity adequacy mechanism: the upper layer is the strategic optimization model for power generators, and the lower layer is the day-ahead market clearing model. Secondly, by using the optimality conditions of the lower model and a series of precise linearization methods, the two-layer models are transformed into several mixed-integer linear programming problems, and the game equilibrium is iteratively solved using a dynamic game framework. Case studies show that, compared to scarcity pricing mechanisms, reliability options can suppress the market power abuse by power generators during high-load periods and lead to a market equilibrium with lower user costs, while the other three mechanisms can only maintain or increase user costs.

articleTitle: Power Control Strategy for Bidirectional Interlinking Converter in Islanded Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In the hybrid AC/DC microgrid with the islanded operation, reasonably controlling the bidirectional interlinking converter (BIC) is the key to realizing mutual power sharing between AC and DC subgrids. Aiming at the problem of frequent switching of BIC operating modes due to small range fluctuation of system power and frequent start-stop due to adding threshold value when real-time eigenvalue is used as the basis of BIC control, an improved power control strategy is proposed, which eliminates the compensation of real-time eigenvalue and adds the threshold as the basis of start-stop judgment, so as to enhance the stability of the system. Meanwhile, different reference values are adopted for various operating conditions of the system to avoid the occurrence of the subgrid deviating from the rated operating conditions due to the different degrees of light and heavy loads between AC and DC subgrids and the mutual aid of power. Finally, the simulation verifies that the strategy can effectively reduce the power loss and achieve smooth operation of the system.

articleTitle: Voltage Prediction of Substation Users with Photovoltaic Based on Weather Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Due to the significant impact of meteorological factors on photovoltaic users, it is necessary to reasonably consider the influence of meteorological factors in voltage prediction in substation users with photovoltaic. This article first analyzes the correlation between meteorological factors and photovoltaic users voltage. Then considers that different meteorological factors have different degrees of correlation with voltage, principal component analysis is used to obtain coupled meteorological factors, cluster the coupled meteorological factors, and finally obtain historical voltage data under different meteorological conditions. The Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) model is selected to predict the user voltage, considering the current weather type. The prediction results indicate that the model using weather classification can provide more accurate voltage prediction and has good practicality.

articleTitle: Short-term Forecasting for Charging Pile and Photovoltaic Loads Based on LSTM-Seq2seq Model in Extreme Weather
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of low prediction accuracy for charging pile (CP) and photovoltaic (PV) load in extreme weathers, a short-term load forecasting model based on the Pearson correlation analysis method and LSTM-Seq2seq network is proposed in this paper. Firstly, meteorological data sets and corresponding load data under extreme weather conditions were filtered using specific meteorological indicators. Next, the meteorological indicators were identified using Pearson correlation analysis, which show a high correlation with the load were selected. Then, the LSTM-Seq2Seq model is used to capture the temporal relationships between the load and the features. Finally, the above features were input into the model to obtain improved short-term load forecasting results. The effectiveness of the model is verified by case studies.

articleTitle: Review and Prospect of Research on Optimization Methods for Load Model Parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: This study provides an overview of the field of power grid safety analysis and simulation technology, focusing on the load model and parameters of the Central China Power Grid. With the help of big data analysis, the study analyzes the patterns of load changes with seasons, regions, and other factors, and conducts precise load modeling and parameter optimization analysis. This study introduces the current research progress in load modeling and points out the new situation faced by load modeling. Then, this study proposes a research framework for generalized integrated power load modeling based on big data, and discusses the research plan in detail. The proposed research framework focuses on addressing two key scientific issues, one is the coordination of accuracy and simplicity of the active load model structure based on big data, and the other is the coordination of time-varying and robust parameters of the load model based on big data. Therefore, this study points out a feasible technical route for establishing a load model based on big data.

articleTitle: Optimized Scheduling of Integrated Energy Systems Considering P2G and Integrated Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: To further improve the integrated energy system (IES) 's renewable energy consumption capacity and limit its CO2 emissions, the paper proposes a two-tier scheduling method considering power-to-gas(P2G) and integrated demand response (IDR). First, a mathematical model of carbon capture and two-stage P2G conversion is constructed, and interruptible loads, transferable loads, and substitutable loads are introduced to participate in the IDR; second, a dynamic pricing strategy is formulated to guide the charging of EVs in an orderly manner; finally, optimal scheduling of the IES is established to minimize the operating cost of the IES in the upper model and minimizing the total charging cost of the EVs in the lower model. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified by setting multiple scenarios for comparison and analysis.

articleTitle: Improving Immediate Wind Forecast and Wind Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Wind forecasting is difficult. Increasing the accuracy of short-term wind forecasts is necessary to maximize the operation of wind farms, their production, and promote their development. The aim of this project is to improve existing techniques for predicting wind speed and the power produced by wind turbines. After an in-depth analysis of wind forecasting techniques, the Kalman filter emerged as a promising method. It is an adaptive method for correcting errors associated with physical forecasting models and can be applied immediately without requiring long training times on historical datasets. While most recent methods rely solely on wind speed forecasts, the addition of other variables such as wind direction could improve model accuracy. Although some approaches, such as artificial neural networks, have been shown to reduce the mean error, the inclusion of directionality in Kalman filter models applied to wind speed or power has not been studied. This paper proposes a new method that models Kalman filters based on differences between raw forecasts from numerical weather prediction models and non-linearly modelled observations of wind speed and direction. For energy forecasting, two methods were developed for cases where wind speed observation data is unavailable. Firstly, the Kalman filter is applied directly to power to estimate bias. Secondly, a technique is introduced where observed power is converted to assumed wind speed using an inverse power curve, enabling filters to function based on wind speed. Historical observation and forecast data from 20 sites in Europe and North America were used to analyze model performance. Several indicators were calculated to quantify the accuracy of different models, including bias, the mean absolute error (MAE), and the root mean square error (RMSE). A first-order polynomial yielded the best results for flow-optimized Kalman filters, while higher-order polynomials applied to power reduced the mean error. Adding directionality improved forecast accuracy across all methods studied.

articleTitle: Integrating Fuzzy Chance Constraints with Operational Mechanisms in Concentrated Solar Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The output of Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) plants often fluctuates due to variations in the Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI). To address this issue, this paper focuses on analyzing the operational mechanisms of CSP plants and introduces a model that incorporates fuzzy chance constraints specifically tailored to these mechanisms; and finally, develops a day-ahead optimal scheduling model. The proposed model is validated by solving case studies, demonstrating its effectiveness in reducing the need for the reserve capacity and thereby saving costs. The numerical results highlight the potential of this approach to enhance the reliability and economic efficiency of CSP plants.

articleTitle: A New Method for AC Voltage Withstand Test of High-Voltage Power Cable Based on Gas-Insulated Line and Distribution Partial Discharge Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The AC withstand voltage test is an effective method to identify the main insulation performance and insulation defects of high-voltage cable. In the paper, gas-insulated line is designed and fabricated to connect the series resonance system with the cable under test. It is filled with SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas with a pressure of 0.35MPa and is suitable for test in limited spaces such as indoor substation. The distributed partial discharge (PD) detection system is developed, which consists of high frequency current transformer, synchronous sensor, detection unit, and communication unit, elastic cloud server, and analysis software. By applying distributed networking, PD detection of terminal and joint along the whole cable length during the AC voltage withstand test can be accomplished simultaneously with high efficiency. In addition, the equivalent time and the equivalent frequency map is proposed for separating different type of detected signals, by which sensitivity and accuracy of PD detection can be improved.

articleTitle: Research on ISOP Inverter System and Its Control Strategy that Can Work under Specific Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The input-series-output-parallel (ISOP) inverter system, which consists of standard DC/AC modules connected in series at the input side and in parallel at the output side, is very suitable for high input voltage as well as high output current applications. This paper points out under no-load conditions, the output power of the entire system is approximately zero. Due to differences between the various modules' losses, the existing control strategies fail, simply because the loss difference cannot be balanced by adjusting the output power of each module, resulting in input voltage of each module differs from each other a lot, which causes the system breaks down. This paper proposes adding an auxiliary input voltage sharing circuit, so that input voltage sharing can be achieved. Finally, the proposed control strategy under no-load conditions were simulated and experimented, the results show that the proposed control strategy is correct.

articleTitle: Transformer Intelligent Diagnosis Method Based on Multi-source Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The state-of-the-art fault diagnosis methods for transformers have some disadvantages, e.g., single information source and low diagnosis accuracy, which result in unreliable judgments. Based on transformer information fusion technology, this paper proposes a fault diagnosis method combining probability extreme learning machine (PELM) and improved Dempster-Shafer (D-S) evidence theory. First, three types of data, including dissolved gas in oil, electrical test, and oil chemical experiment, are selected as the input characteristics for fault diagnosis. Furthermore, the method of relative deterioration degree is adopted for preprocessing. Then, the improved extreme learning machine is used to convert the preliminary diagnosis results into a probability distribution matrix. Afterwards, the improved D-S evidence theory algorithm is applied to fuse multiple evidence bodies to achieve comprehensive diagnosis of transformers, which makes the diagnosis results more accurate. Experimental results show that the fault diagnosis accuracy rate of the method proposed is 98.27%. The real-life fault data provided by a certain maintenance company have been tested to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method and the performance of the proposed method is analyzed.

articleTitle: A Design Method of DC-link Capacitor for Three-Phase SPWM Rectifier Under Asymmetric Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The instantaneous active power and DC-link voltage of three-phase SPWM rectifiers can have the components of double fundamental frequency under asymmetric grid faults, affecting the system reliability and power quality. Firstly, the instantaneous active power characteristics of three-phase SPWM rectifiers both on the AC and DC sides are analyzed quantitatively, and the expression of double fundamental frequency component of the DC-link voltage is derived. Next, the most common asymmetric grid fault, single phase-to-ground fault, is considered through introducing a voltage drop coefficient. Then, the influence of single-phase voltage drop coefficient on the DC-link capacitor is analyzed. And the limit value of the DC-link capacitance is obtained, meanwhile considering the third harmonic constraint of the grid current. Finally, the simulation verifications are carried out, and the results have proven the correctness of the theoretical analysis in the paper.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch for Receiving-End Power Grid with Offshore Wind Farm Clusters Considering Peaking Compensation and Cost Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: After large-scale offshore wind farms clusters are connected to the grid, the generation of thermal units is compressed at the receiving-end of the grid, decreasing the motivation of thermal units participating in peak regulation. This paper proposes an optimal dispatch model for wind-thermal-storage peak regulation considering peaking compensation and cost sharing. To encourage each subject of the receiving-end grid to participate in the peak regulation, the wind-thermal-storage peaking compensation and cost allocation method is proposed. Then, the wind-fire-storage peak regulation dispatch model considering peaking compensation and cost sharing is proposed. The objective function is to maximize the total revenue of the system. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified by a simulation validation of an actual receiving-end grid.

articleTitle: A New Fault Location Method for Modern Distribution Network Based on System Parameters Estimation and Self-correction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The parameters of a distribution network are subject to changes due to factors such as weather conditions and load variations. The limited installation of sensing devices and data transmission delays make it difficult to obtain accurate real-time parameters of the distribution network, thereby affecting the accuracy of traditional fault location methods. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fault location method for distribution networks that dynamically adjusts the fault location model with parameter variations, based on the self-correction technology of a digital twin model of the distribution network. Additionally, a digital twin platform was developed using a digital twin server and a real-time simulation platform (RTDS), achieving synchronous operation of the physical model and the digital twin model of the distribution network in real-time. In the case study simulations, the proposed digital twin-based fault location method was validated using the digital twin platform. The results show that this method can correct distribution network parameters in real-time under various system operating conditions, significantly improving the speed and accuracy of fault location in the distribution network.

articleTitle: Energy Supply Scheme for UAV Relay Base Station Based on Power over Fiber Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: We propose an energy supply scheme for UAV relay base station based on power over fiber technology, and conduct preliminary experiments and field verification. The proposed scheme utilizes a 500m multimode fiber to transmit a high-power laser, combined with a photoelectric conversion module, to achieve a 2W power output from a single photocell in a 1*19 photocell array at the relay base station. The scheme is not subject to electromagnetic interference, and it can feed power to the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) relay base station 24 hours a day, which provides experimental support for breaking through the bottleneck of UAV energy supply in the smart grid.

articleTitle: Edge Computing for Microgrid via MATLAB Embedded Coder and Low-Cost Smart Meters
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In this paper, an edge computing-based machine-learning study is conducted for solar inverter power forecasting and droop control in a remote microgrid. The machine learning models and control algorithms are directly deployed on an edge-computing device (a smart meter-concentrator) in the microgrid rather than on a cloud server at the far-end control center, reducing the communication time the inverters need to wait. Experimental results on an ARM-based smart meter board demonstrate the feasibility and correctness of the proposed approach by comparing against the results on the desktop PC.

articleTitle: Non-Functional Electrical Scene Extraction Method Considering Spatiotemporal Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In recent years, the power grid structure and load type have undergone profound changes, and the requirements for power quality have gradually increased, and the characteristics of user-side load, including reactive power and power factors, have also changed. Therefore, in order to better optimize reactive power allocation, this paper proposes a method to extract inactive power scenes considering temporal and spatial correlation, and conducts experiments based on the operation data of three transformers in a certain area of Shanghai. The results show that the proposed algorithm based on LE-GMM for extracting the typical day scene of inactive electricity considering the temporal and spatial correlation has a good ability to fit the actual operation scene.

articleTitle: Design and Research of A Low-harmonic Marine Frequency Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The marine frequency converter uses the pulse width modulation, and the power supply side produces the harmonic wave, which causes the electrical network waveform distortion, and leads to the electrical energy quality question, even interferes with other equipment the work. In this paper, a low harmonic marine frequency converter is proposed. We replace the uncontrolled rectifier circuit by a three-phase Vienna rectifier circuit, which can effectively and actively suppress the harmonics on the power supply side. So that the total voltage distortion rate can be lower than 2%. Meanwhile, it can reduce the size of the input filter and improve the power density of the frequency converter. A 4kVA frequency converter is developed, and the experimental results verify the feasibility of the technology.

articleTitle: Information Modeling of Distributed Electrochemical Energy Storage Shared Operation Based on Holographic Features
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The common information model (CIM) and the packages and classes inside the model do not include the relevant contents in the field of distributed energy storage (DES), which has certain limitations. Moreover, there are many kinds of electrochemical DES, and there are many problems such as incompatible communication protocols, incompatible monitoring systems, different principles and communication methods of the underlying monitoring devices, and no uniform standards for data storage. For this reason, this paper combines the electrochemical DES distribution spatiotemporal characteristics and the shared storage operation mode and establishes a CIM description model for the state of DES and co-generation system, which describes the classes, properties and their interrelationships. The model consists of DES modules of different scales, and applications such as model building and bi-directional engineering are carried out under the Rational Rose platform, and forward engineering is used to verify the consistency of the data transmission of the established information model.

articleTitle: Pilot Protection Based on Hamming Distance for Transmission Line Connected to Renewable Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Affected by the converter control strategy, the fault characteristics of the renewable energy power supply are essentially distinctive from the traditional synchronous power supply, resulting in the deterioration of the traditional protection device action performance and the risk of rejection. In response to the above issues, the paper studies the fault current waveform difference between the renewable energy power supply and the traditional synchronous power supply, uses the Hamming distance to measure the current waveform difference, and proposes protection principle based on Hamming distance. The simulation results and fault recording data indicate that the Hamming distance can accurately distinguish the faults in and out of the zone in various fault scenarios, has good resistance to transition resistance and system noise, and can be applied to scenarios with weak output of renewable energy.

articleTitle: A Study on Detection of Pollution Status of Porcelain Insulators for Power Transmission Based on Improved YOLOv8-seg
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Porcelain insulators are crucial components of insulation in power transmission lines and are still widely used in online applications. As the operational time increases, dust accumulation on the insulator surface leads to the formation of polluted insulators, resulting in a decrease in the external insulation level and increasing the risk of flashover under wet conditions, leading to widespread power outages. Current non-contact detection methods suffer from low detection efficiency and poor accuracy, making it difficult to intuitively and effectively assess the pollution status of insulators. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for detecting the pollution status of porcelain insulators based on improved YOLOv8-seg. Firstly, the YOLOv8-seg entity segmentation model is improved by adding the CBAM attention mechanism to focus on key feature information and enhance detection accuracy. Secondly, the SPPF module is upgraded to the SPPFCSPC module to optimize multi-scale object detection accuracy. Thirdly, the standard convolution (Conv) module is replaced with the Alterable Kernel Convolution (AKConv) module to reduce computational complexity and network overhead. Furthermore, the insulator region is further segmented, and image processing and filtering techniques are employed to extract color features from the insulator surface. Finally, the color features of insulators with different degrees of pollution under varying humidity are analyzed, and a pollution status detection method for insulators is proposed. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method meets the requirements of practical inspection in terms of accuracy and speed, providing valuable insights for insulator pollution status detection work.

articleTitle: The Impact of Operational Constraints on the Uniqueness of Locational Marginal Price: Simulation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Over the past two decades, Locational Marginal Prices (LMP) theory has not only been continuously revised and developed in large-scale applications but also has become an essential component of the construction of China's electricity market, so researching the uniqueness of LMP is crucial. This paper first briefly analyzes the nodal pricing mechanism and uniqueness of solutions for the Security Constrained Economic Dispatch (SCED) problem and its dual problem. Subsequently, a full-time spot market clearing optimization model which considers relevant operational constraints is established, mainly used for computing the marginal nodal prices for power units, and a method for determining price multiplicities suitable for general cases is proposed. Lastly, numerical results show that line thermal capacity constraints and N-1 security constraint impacts the uniqueness of prices.

articleTitle: Voltage Characteristic Analysis and Operation Optimization of Distribution Network Considering Source Load Uncertaint
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In order to deal with the problem of voltage overlimit and network loss increase caused by random fluctuation of load, wind power and photovoltaic power output in distribution network, the voltage characteristics analysis and optimization of distributed power supply were carried out. Firstly, the output uncertainty of distributed power supply is modeled, and the influence of uncertainty on power grid is analyzed by probabilistic power flow calculation. Then, taking the network loss minimization as the objective function, the mathematical optimization model is established, and the particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to comprehensively optimize the voltage of the root node, the energy storage output and the reactive power compensator output. Through the simulation calculation of IEEE33-node distribution network, it is verified that the control scheme can effectively reduce the network loss while guaranteeing the voltage quality. The results show that the comprehensive optimization strategy can significantly reduce the network loss and improve the operation efficiency of the power distribution network on the basis of ensuring the voltage stability of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Fault Characteristics Analysis of the Modular Multilevel Converter-type Multi-Port Solid-State Transformer under Different Grounding Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC)-type multi-port solid-state transformers (SSTs) have been widely utilized in the AC/DC hybrid distribution networks. Analyzing its fault characteristics under various grounding methods is crucial for optimizing system design and operation. Firstly, the equivalent fault circuits are established for the single phase-to-ground fault and the positive pole ground fault, when the transformer uses the Yg/Δ configuration. Then, the characteristic of the positive pole ground fault is investigated, under a Δ/Yg grounding transformer configuration. Finally, several simulation tests were carried out in MATLAB, and the simulation results verified the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis in this paper.

articleTitle: Short-Term PV Power Prediction Method Based on Weather Classification and TCN-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: For the purpose of improving the prediction accuracy of short-term PV power under different weather conditions, a short-term PV power prediction method based on weather classification combined with temporal convolutional network-attention mechanism combination model is proposed. Firstly, Spearman and Kendall correlation coefficients are used to select the main meteorological factors affecting PV power, including total solar irradiance, direct irradiance, global horizontal irradiance, temperature and relative humidity. Then, the K-means++ algorithm was employed to classify the historical PV data into three types: sunny, cloudy and rainy days. Finally, based on the temporal feature extraction ability of time-convolutional network and the ability of attention mechanism to highlight the key features, the combined time-convolutional network-attention mechanism model is established. Simulation results show that the proposed method is able to improve the accuracy of short-term PV power prediction under different weather conditions with strong adaptability.

articleTitle: Wearable Detection Application of Protective Equipment for Live Working Based on YOLOv9
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of relying on manual supervision and low degree of automation in the wearing of safety protective equipment for non-outage workers in the power sector, this paper proposes an automatic detection model based on improved YOLOv9. Firstly, a self-calibrating convolution is designed, which can explicitly expand the field of view of each convolution layer, thus enriching the output features and enhancing the feature extraction ability of the model for targets in complex environments. Secondly, the model down-sampling module is improved. In order to reduce the loss of information caused by the down-sampling stage, a down-sampling module based on wavelet transform is designed to maximize the integrity of information. Finally, through experiments on the self-built live working safety wearable data set, the average accuracy mean is used as the model evaluation index, and compared with the existing target detection algorithm. The experimental results show that the im-proved algorithm proposed in this paper has a significant improvement in detection accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: The Study on the Influence of Electric Fields on Oil- Paper Griffin Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Moisture plays a crucial role in the aging and electrical strength of transformer oil-paper insulation. Currently, no sensor technology exists for directly measuring moisture content in transformer paper; instead, calculations rely on the Griffin curve for indirect assessments. This study explores how electric fields affect the moisture balance of oil-paper insulation at 80°C. The findings reveal that the electric field hinders moisture migration, and with increasing electric field strength, the moisture content in both oil and paper rises significantly. At 0 kV/mm, the results are consistent, while at 25 kV/mm, the average moisture content in the paper corresponding to the same moisture level in the oil increases by 32.92%. Moreover, macroscopic force analysis and microscopic molecular simulations further substantiate the experimental findings, offering insights for refining the moisture balance curve of oil-paper insulation under multi-physical field influences.

articleTitle: Analysis of China's Green Electricity Trading Issues and a Market Clearing Model Considering Green Electricity Participation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: China has established a green electricity trading mechanism. Wind and photovoltaic power generation companies can bundle their energy with green power certificates and sell them to electricity users. Through green electricity trading, electricity users have achieved consumption of renewable energy. However, there are still many problems with the green electricity trading mechanism at present. In the actual transaction organization process, green electricity trading is also organized separately from conventional energy trading. This article summarizes the current situation of green electricity trading in China and analyzes the problems that exist in green electricity trading. Finally, a centralized bidding transaction for all types of power sources was established with the participation of green power.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Low-Voltage Distribution Network Based on Photovoltaic Energy Storage Integrated Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: With the development of distributed photovoltaic business, user-based photovoltaic energy storage integrated equipment is being connected to the low-voltage distribution network. However, this phenomenon will lead to the weak end of the distribution network voltage overlimit and other problems, seriously affect the healthy operation of the distribution network. In this paper, a two-layer optimal scheduling model based on PV and energy storage cluster is proposed. The upper layer uses benders algorithm to calculate the active power output of photovoltaic energy storage nodes to optimize the energy storage balance, and the lower layer uses particle swarm optimization to calculate the reactive power output to optimize the node voltage balance. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is verified by an 18-nodes simulation in a rural area.

articleTitle: Control Strategy Based on Second-Order Linear Active Disturbance Rejection for Flexible DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of large fluctuations of instantaneous power and DC side voltage and current caused by asymmetric faults on the AC side of flexible DC grid, and then affecting the stable operation of the system, a station-level control strategy for flexible DC grids based on Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control (LADRC) is proposed. Based on the second-order LADRC theory, the positive and negative sequence current inner loop controllers are designed, respectively. Finally, a four-terminal flexible DC grid model is built based on PSCAD/EMTDC platform for example analysis. The results show that the proposed control strategy can not only reduce the fluctuation of instantaneous power and DC side voltage and current, but also decrease the adverse effect of negative sequence current on system operation.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategy of Non-isolated Low voltage Flexible Interconnected Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Under the background of the construction of new power systems, flexible interconnection technology has been widely applied. In order to suppress the circulating current after the closure of the substation, isolated flexible interconnected inverters are often used. Therefore, there are problems such as large device size, low efficiency, and high cost, which are not conducive to promotion. In order to solve the above problems. To solve the problems of large volume, low efficiency, and high cost of low-voltage flexible interconnection devices, this paper proposes a non-isolated transformer topology. And based on this topology, a zero sequence circulating current control method is proposed to suppress the zero sequence circulating current after canceling the isolation transformer. Finally, through simulation verification, the topology and zero sequence circulating current suppression strategy proposed in this paper can effectively suppress the zero sequence circulating current, reduce equipment volume, improve equipment efficiency, and reduce equipment costs.

articleTitle: Research on the Schedulability Prediction Method of Electric Vehicle Cluster Based on CNN-BiLSTM-Attention and Model Coupling Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Under the background of dual-carbon, aiming at the difficulty of flexible scheduling and the accuracy of schedulability prediction of massive electrical vehicle (EV) after grid connection, a CNN-BiLSTM-Attention and model coupling driven schedulability prediction method considering the stopping characteristics of EV cluster is proposed. Firstly, the convolutional neural network (CNN) is used to fully extract the detailed features of EV stopping data, and then the bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) network is cascaded to bidirectionally mine the spatio-temporal characteristics of EV stopping data, and the attention mechanism is integrated to dynamically allocate weights for the stopping features to improve the prediction accuracy of EV stopping parameters. Secondly, considering the natural aggregation of charging stations, an EV cluster is constructed by aggregating individual EVs based on Minkowski summation, and it is simplified as a generalized energy storage (GES) device. Finally, the capacity and power boundary of the GES model are described according to the prediction results of the EV cluster stop parameters, which can effectively take into account the user's energy consumption law and quantify the EV cluster schedulability. The simulation results show that compared with the single-driven schedulability prediction method, the combined method can further clarify the energy consumption behavior of EV users, reduce the model dimension, and realize the accurate description of the schedulability of EV clusters.

Author Keywords: bidirectional long short-term memory neural network

articleTitle: Optimization for Penalty Cost in Electricity Trading Using Energy Dispatching between Aggregators
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: In the future retail electricity market, deviation penalties will be one of the largest challenges faced by energy aggregators, directly impacting their profitability. With the objective of minimizing the penalty cost, an energy deviation optimization method is proposed to optimize the assessed energy deviation amount with a mutual energy dispatching strategy among energy aggregators. The model considers the status of interruptible loads, expected interruption upper limits, interruption quantities, and the transfer of electricity of the aggregators under both day-ahead and real-time scenarios. Simulations conducted with different energy aggregators, representing different load types, demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively reduce energy deviations and associated penalty costs, with an average reduction of 16.6% in total costs compared to that without mutual energy dispatching.

articleTitle: Identification and Localization of Partial Discharge in Power Cable Based on Phase Space Vector and Energy Criterion
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Identification and localization of partial discharge (PD) are important part of condition monitoring and diagnosis of power cable to ensure their reliable operation. In this paper, a PD detection system is developed, which consists of high frequency current transformer, signal conditioning circuit, data acquisition unit, and analysis software. The phase space vector method is proposed for identifying the type of detected signals. By calculating the correlation coefficient between the phase space vector graph of real-time detected signal and typical signals, the type of real-time detected signal can be determined by which signal identification can be realized with less data calculation and high efficiency. For realizing the automatic PD localization in power cable, the energy criterion method is proposed for determination of the time delay between detected PD pulses. The developed PD detection system and proposed methods are applied in field tests, it is verified that the insulation defect in power cable can be identified quickly and localized automatically.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Operating Economy of SVC and SVG based on Accurate Dynamic Losses Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The losses calculation model for reactive power compensation devices in substations is relatively crude. It is based solely on the rated losses parameters provided by the equipment manufacturers, which makes it difficult to accurately reflect the losses of reactive power compensation devices under actual operating conditions. It is also challenging to fully understand the variation of losses under various operational strategies. To address this issue, this paper discusses two widely used reactive power compensation devices in substations—SVC and SVG, and proposes dynamic losses models for both SVC and SVG. Simulation is conducted in Simulink. It is demonstrated that the accurate dynamic operation losses can more realistically reflect the losses of reactive power compensation devices and provide data support for formulating operational strategies, compared to traditional calculation methods.

articleTitle: Smart Grid Power Load Prediction Method Based on VMD-TCN-BiGRU-TSAM
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: To address the challenges of high volatility and low prediction accuracy in smart grid power load data, we propose a novel power load prediction method that integrates Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN), Bi-directional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU), and a Temporal Self-Attention Mechanism (TSAM). Our approach begins with the application of VMD to decompose the smart grid power load data, resulting in subsequences characterized by stronger regularity. We then utilize the Maximum Information Coefficient (MIC) to identify weather factors that exhibit a strong correlation with power load variations. These selected weather factors, along with historical load data and the decomposed subsequences, are reorganized to form a comprehensive new load dataset. Each subsequence is subsequently input into the combined TCN-BiGRU model, where the feature vectors derived from this process are classified using an enhanced BiGRU model that incorporates the Temporal Self- Attention Mechanism (TSAM) to enhance prediction performance. Finally, we aggregate the predicted values from all subsequences to obtain a complete set of predicted load values. We validate our proposed method using real power load data from a station area in a city in China. The results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves superior prediction accuracy compared to traditional forecasting methods, thereby contributing to more effective optimization of power dispatch in smart grids.

articleTitle: Equivalent Modeling and Real-Time Simulation Research on Large-Scale Photovoltaic Cluster Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: With the rapid construction of large-scale new energy, large-scale real-time simulation technology faces more severe challenges. This paper focuses on the study of large-scale photovoltaic clusters with a capacity of tens of millions of kilowatts, via HVDC transmission systems. It conducts equivalent modeling and real-time simulation experiments for clusters consisting of thousands or even tens of thousands of photovoltaic generating units. Firstly, the paper introduces the general networking structure of large-scale photovoltaic cluster systems and the control strategies for photovoltaic generating units. Subsequently, it proposes the establishment of an equivalent simulation model for the collection line and a hard-ware-in-the-loop simulation test method, and establishes a real-time simulation comparison test platform. Finally, based on the RTDS platform, a computing resource allocation scheme for the photovoltaic collection line subsystem is designed, and real-time simulation model comparison experiments are conducted before and after the equivalence of photovoltaic generating units, providing a reference case for the application of system-level real-time simulation technology.

articleTitle: A Data Cleaning Method for Power Transformer Situational Awareness Based on RANSAC and Improved IForest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Interference from operational environments and data acquisition devices can introduce noise into transformer monitoring systems, compromising the accuracy of equipment status analysis. To address this, enhancing data quality through effective cleaning techniques is crucial. This paper proposes an innovative data cleaning approach for power transformers, combining the Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) algorithm with an enhanced Isolation Forest (IForest) model. By leveraging unsupervised learning strategies, the method focuses on analyzing dissolved gas data in transformer oil. RANSAC is employed to establish a mathematical model reflecting gas component relationships, based on the gas content ratio principle. Meanwhile, the improved IForest learns from historical data to construct a data cleaning model, which is then used for automated dataset cleaning. Experimental results confirm the method's effectiveness in mitigating the impact of noisy and unreliable data on detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimization of Energy Interaction between air Conditioning Load and Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: As the number of distributed resources increases, the operation of the grid tends to be a more flexible distributed, and interactive model. As the most important forms of distributed resources, electric vehicles and air conditioning loads have the property of coupling time and space and play a key role in improving the economic operation level of power grids. This paper proposes a coordinated optimization strategy for electric vehicles and air conditioning load in the distribution network, aiming to improve the economic operation efficiency and power supply reliability of the power network through intelligent energy dispatching. The study considers the charge-discharge flexibility of electric vehicles and the adjustment potential of air conditioning load, and realizes the effective regulation of power grid load in different seasons and different periods through the actual case of a residential area in Shanghai. By guiding electric vehicles to charge or reverse discharge during off-peak periods, the peak load during peak air conditioning usage is reduced and the peak-valley difference is reduced.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Risk Prediction Technology for Overhead Lines under Cold Wave Weather Using Line Tension Data
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of icing breakage and tower collapse of transmission lines under cold wave weather and the lack of historical data and unknown mechanism of icing, this paper proposes a risk prediction model for overhead lines under cold wave weather based on the deep learning of line tension data from the perspective of transmission line mechanics. First, the line tension threshold calculation model for each voltage level is established to estimate the line tension risk threshold under cold wave weather. Aiming at the characteristics of the cold wave weather sample data, the sample extension dataset is trained using an adversarial generative network. Then, based on the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, a predictive learning model is built with the expanded time-series data samples to study the mapping relationship between the line pull increment of linear towers and meteorological data under cold wave weather. Using an example from a province in China, it is demonstrated that the sample enhancement algorithm can improve the risk prediction performance through sample learning; compared with other common prediction models, the tension prediction model based on multi-model fusion has better prediction stability.

articleTitle: A Fault Location Method for Modern Distribution Network Based on Fault State Estimation by Hybrid Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The micro-phasor measurement unit (PMU) provides a solid measurement foundation for further upgrades in distribution automation. However, the current limited number of PMUs in the power grid cannot meet the demands of traditional fault location methods in distribution networks. To address this issue, a fault location method based on hybrid measurement state estimation is proposed, integrating PMUs with smart meters and utilizing a multiple state estimation method based on virtual nodes. First, the measurement information from PMUs and smart meters is input into the fault state estimator through equivalent transformation. Then, the network is divided into different regions using PMUs. Fault currents are calculated based on the state estimation results to narrow down the fault search area and reduce computational complexity. To identify the fault location within the region, multiple specific fault topologies are created by setting additional virtual fault nodes, and multiple state estimations are performed to compute the weighted measurement residuals used to determine the fault location. Finally, simulation tests are conducted in a real-time digital simulation (RTDS) system. The results show that the proposed method can accurately and effectively locate faults under different fault scenarios and has good robustness against measurement errors.

articleTitle: Optimization Dispatch Method for Offshore Wind Farm Clusters Considering Wake Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The wake effect between adjacent offshore wind farms introduces a power-shifting capability that can be harnessed to enhance the ability to participate in grid peak-shaving dispatch. This paper establishes an adjacent-farm power time-shift model that accounts for the wake effect among offshore wind farms and reduces the deviation between wind farm output and grid dispatch plans by joint energy storage charging and discharging. An optimization dispatch model integrated with energy storage systems is proposed based on the characteristic of adjacent-farm power time-shift. The objective is to minimize the total costs, including wind curtailment penalties, output deviation costs, and energy storage operation costs, while adhering to constraints on wind power output, energy storage operation, and power shift capabilities. The proposed method is validated through simulations using an actual offshore wind farm cluster with an integrated energy storage system. The results demonstrate that this method effectively leverages the power-shifting potential between adjacent offshore wind farms, reduces energy storage power operation and wind curtailment costs, and enables the offshore wind farm cluster to effectively track grid peak-shaving dispatch plans.

articleTitle: Graph Learning Method for Voltage Area Partition in Inaccurate Multiphase Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Power distribution networks are rapidly evolving into large-scale, highly complex, and topologically variable active distribution networks (ADNs). In such ADNs, voltage issues are serious and thus the distributed or decentralized voltage control tends to be called for, whose effectiveness is critically dependent on the proper partitioning of the network into multiple sub-networks, a.k.a., voltage area partition (VAP). Existing partitioning methods are focused on three-phase balanced systems with known line parameters, making them less applicable to real-world distribution networks. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a data-driven VAP method, which can perceive voltage sensitivity from the historical operation data without need of precise distribution line parameters while simultaneously assigning buses into clusters by designing a physics-informed graph neural network architecture. In particular, a phase-completing layer is developed to convert a phase-missing bus to a three-phase bus, which can fairly evaluate the voltage cohesiveness of different buses. Simulation in the modified IEEE 123 bus system demonstrates that the proposed method yields partitioning results with higher voltage cohesiveness compared to benchmark methods.

articleTitle: A Multi-temporal Deep Learning Architecture for Smart Retrofitting of Buildings in Service
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Given the numerous studies on how to make buildings smarter through smart devices, there is a need for more research on retrofitting large buildings with legacy equipment and systems. We propose a deep learning based cyber-physical control solution for smart retrofitting of buildings in service. Specifically, our solution first collects real-time operational data without interrupting the operation of the original control system, and then utilizes the LSTM-CNN prediction model to learn the multi-scene control strategy embedded in the historical data. Based on this model, intelligent retrofitting of many large buildings can be realized, thus significantly reducing the manpower required for manual operation and maintenance. The model was experimented using real data from the HVAC system of the T3 terminal building of Beijing Capital International Airport, and the results show that the proposed solution can be used in conjunction with existing equipment to accomplish the smart retrofit and can effectively replace manual control.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Electrical Information System Network Security Verification Method
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Factory and main stations must be secured from multiple angles as part of the power information system network asset security. Proposing a networked asset security verification program that satisfies security criteria for power systems is imperative, given the current norms and standards. In addition to providing clear security verification criteria and comprehensive work recommendations for the safety certification of networked assets, this article normalizes and standardizes the security verification procedure. To facilitate quick information exchange between the manufacturing station and the verification device, the power system's network asset security verification model has been built to layer up the information collection layer and identify the storage and safety verification layers. The verification device is designed with modular thinking in mind. Regression techniques ensure the collected content is accurate, and a multi-layer random forest algorithm is employed to detect security verification irregularities. The power system's networked asset security verification device has significantly increased safety verification efficiency and has the prerequisites for widespread use. Ultimately, experimental verification and real-world engineering applications were conducted.
