articleTitle: A Credible Regulating Capacity Evaluation Method of Virtual Control Units in Frequency Response
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: By employing virtual power plant technology, various types of distributed energy resources on the distribution side can be aggregated into a virtual control unit, allowing for direct participation in the frequency response of the power system. This aggregates effectively addresses the shortage of frequency regulation resources. The uncertainty associated with operational states and user behavior results in time-varying capabilities of individual distributed energy resources, leading to probabilistic characteristics in the adjustment capabilities of the virtual control unit. Consequently, it is essential to develop an evaluation method for the credible frequency response capacity of the virtual control unit, which will provide foundational information for power system operation and control tasks. To accurately simulate the operational states of distributed energy resources, individual models are constructed based on their operational characteristics and user behavior. Additionally, a frequency response capacity evaluation model for these individual resources is established, taking into account both resource characteristics and operational constraints. For the chosen resources, the feasible region is graphically represented to facilitate analysis, thereby forming an analytical calculation method for the frequency response capacity of individual resources. Key parameters involved in the aggregation process are identified, and an evaluation model for the credible frequency response capacity of the virtual control unit is developed using confidence levels and Monte Carlo simulations, based on the probabilistic distribution characteristics of these parameters. The feasibility and correctness of the proposed method are validated through Monte Carlo simulations across multiple scenarios. Furthermore, the simulation results allow for the assessment of the credible frequency response capacity of the virtual control unit at various confidence levels.

articleTitle: Risk Assessment of Distributed PV Microgrids Under Cyber Attacks based on CNN-AE
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The widespread application of smart grid technology and numerous Internet of Things (IoT) devices expose microgrid vulnerability to various cyber attacks. Moreover, the complex interactions and implicit risk propagation within the system pose challenges in accessing the risk from cyber attacks. To this end, we propose a risk assessment method for distributed PV microgrids under cyber attacks. This program employs an autoencoder (AE) architecture where convolutional neural networks (CNN) serve as the intermediate layer to extract the local features of data exchange from adjacent nodes. The AE conducts unsupervised learning using power data under normal operating conditions, thus performing risk assessment by evaluating the reconstruction errors. To validate the proposed method, we conducted training on the algorithm using historical data and the topology of a real scenario of a distributed photovoltaic microgrid and tested the risk assessment with various fake data injection attacks (FDIA) and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks.

articleTitle: Real-Time Exchange of IEC 61850 Sample Values over 5G for Grid Monitoring and Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: High-quality real-time data from the grid is essential for data-driven real-time operations. With a geographically widespread grid, there is a lot of interest in using mobile networks for communications to avoid the need to invest in and operate an additional communication network, but the quality and reliability of the mobile network need to be sufficient. In this paper, we investigate configurations of a 5G testbed for transmission of IEC 61850 sample values, in particular with respect to achieving low latency. Considering that different grid use cases have different traffic patterns we show how the performance can vary and the impact of adjusting multiple network parameters. The results demonstrate that the interaction between different mechanisms is complex, but there are important gains to be made from good UE specific parameter configurations.

articleTitle: Research on the Evaluation of the Fit of Electricity Market Development Planning Based on Cloud Model
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The modernization of China's governance system and governance capacity has put forward the requirement of better serving economic and social development for the reform of electricity marketization, and it is necessary to establish indicators and methods for evaluating the electricity market from the perspective of economic and social development. In this paper, by analysing the need for the power market to adapt to the new power system and the real needs of the power market construction, we constructed a fit assessment system between the power market and economic and social development, and proposed a fit assessment model using a combination of the cloud model and the TOPSIS method. Through the transformation of the approximation of the ideal solution ordering method, the relative closeness between the cloud models is used to characterise the degree of fit for evaluation. The analysis of the final arithmetic example shows that the degree of fit between the development plan and the development objectives of an electricity market in a province is not high.

articleTitle: Assessing the Security and Architectural Frameworks of Self-Driving Cars in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: This review aims at presenting a clear understanding of AVs in smart cities, more specifically in terms of technological development, inherent challenges, and social impacts. LiDAR sensors and the communication protocols essential for improving the navigation and safety of AVs in urban areas are explored. The review brings together recent studies and notes the resultant adversities of the AV sensor system with respect to the weather impact as well as the need to strengthen protection against cyber-crimes. Other key areas of concern include road traffic control, traffic flow reduction, energy conservation, and changes in the transport system usage within urban areas. In incorporating various aspects related to the AV integration, the review highlights the role of policy makers, researchers and industry players, and stresses the need for regulatory framework, societal acceptance, and design of interaction between human and computers as crucial in the development of AVs. AVs hold the potential of enabling smarter, safer, and sustainable cities worldwide in the future and the consequent growth of sensor technology and communication networks for AV technologies are prospective for urban mobility.

articleTitle: Developing Clean Coal Technology in Industrial Sector Toward Smart Grid Decarbonization
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Under the background of smart grid, the clean and efficient utilization of coal is of great significance to the sustainable development of power system. Industrial industry and equipment are important application scenarios of coal, so this paper first summarizes the current situation of coal utilization in industrial fields at home and abroad. In order to realize the decarbonization of smart grid, this paper indicates the efficient and clean utilization path of coal in the key industry and industrial field according to the carbon reduction process in the production process. Finally, the positive influence of efficient coal utilization on smart grid construction is analyzed.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Model Predictive Control and Heuristics in Building Energy Management
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in the electricity grid underscores the critical need for advanced energy management systems in residential settings. Traditional energy management systems are limited in handling the complexity and dynamism of energy systems, thus hindering efficient energy utilization in buildings. This study conducts a novel evaluation of Model Predictive Control versus traditional rule-based systems within a lab-based energy management system prototype for households. The experimental setup consisted of a bidirectional power supply, lithium-ion batteries, and a programmable logic controller. All systems were rigorously tested over consecutive seven-day periods, taking into account photovoltaic supply, electricity demand, and pricing to optimize energy management and reduce overall electricity costs. The results demonstrate the superior efficiency of the advanced control strategy in minimizing electricity costs compared to traditional controllers, which struggle with the complexity of sector coupling and dynamic energy environments. This research offers new insights into the practical viability and performance of Model Predictive Control in real-world settings, showcasing its potential for advanced energy management and emphasizing the importance of open standards in interface development for future advancements. Recognizing the necessity for comprehensive solutions, model- and data-driven approaches can integrate households as active participants in the dynamic energy system, enabling real-time adaptation to fluctuating grid conditions. By effectively communicating the advantages of advanced control technologies to policymakers, energy providers, and homeowners, we can encourage broader adoption and unlock their potential for creating a more sustainable, efficient, and cost-effective energy future.

articleTitle: Joint Nest Deployment and Path Planning for Multi-U AV Power Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)-based intelligent inspection is considered a promising technology for future inspection systems. In this paper, we study a multi-UAV autonomous power inspection system, where a set of UAVs fly towards the towers to take photos, i.e., collecting data on insulators. We provide a joint design aiming to minimize nest construction cost and total inspection time by jointly optimizing nest deploying and UAVs path while satisfying the constraint of maximum UAV flight time. However, the formulated problem is a multi-objective coupled problem, and the algorithm's complexity increases hierarchically with the number of towers. To solve such issues, we first decompose the problem into a nest deployment sub-problem and a UAVs path planning sub-problem. Then a joint optimization scheme is proposed, including a sparrow search K-means (SS-Kmeans) algorithm for nest deployment and an adaptive pheromone concentration ant colony (APCAC) algorithm for UAVs path planning. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can effectively balance the relationship between UAV inspection efficiency and cost, and the performance of the proposed method significantly outperforms the baselines.

articleTitle: Enhancing Port and Maritime Cybersecurity Through AI - Enabled Threat Detection and Response
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The maritime industry remains exposed to cyber threats due to the old systems and depends on the existing, unequally distributed cyber security measures. This function hinges on the operations of the global ports and shipping facilities that assist in the smooth flow of commerce. To enhance the effectiveness of threat identification and management, this article aims at evaluating how the application of Artificial Intelligence algorithms in the sphere of ship operation and ports' security may enhance marine cyber protection. AI technologies also offer effective and efficient threat detection and response solutions in real-time utilizing projections. The study also points out the weaknesses that should not be overlooked, presents an overview of cybersecurity in the marine industry and discusses integration of Artificial Intelligence to plan a comprehensive cybersecurity strategy. In a way, the study shows the positive impact that AI-based approaches can have on the safety and stability of the marine industry by examining specific examples of the use cases of AI. The report also talks on functional, ethical and legal concerns about artificial intelligence for such scenarios. This suggests that the integration of AI in the Maritime cybersecurity structures increases the alert system for hostile intrusions and strengthens the overall defense of crucial infrastructure of global business chains.

articleTitle: Low Carbon Economic Dispatch of Power System Based on Multi-point Grid Connection of Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: A low-carbon economic operation strategy is proposed for complex AC-DC distribution system formed by offshore grid, hydrogen energy system and receiving-end grid. This method can minimize operating cost and carbon emission of system under the uncertainty output of RES by using dispatchable region (DR) of offshore wind farms (OWFs) with hydrogen production (HP) and distributionally robust optimization (DRO). A method is proposed based on dynamic programming and computational geometry theory which can quantify the variable load regulation potential at the junction point under the output uncertainty of OWFs. Furthermore, a low carbon economic operation model for AC-DC distribution system with the lowest expected operation cost, maintenance and wind abandonment as the objective function is established. Finally, a study based on the IEEE 30-bus system with 11 nodes offshore grid demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the overall operating cost and carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Crowd Management Through Potential Field-Based Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: This study introduces an innovative approach to crowd management through advanced computational modeling and visualization techniques. By leveraging the capabilities of Python and Matplotlib, we developed a comprehensive framework that segments a defined area into a grid, simulating crowd density through variable point distributions. This method incorporates realistic scenarios by integrating weighted regions to represent areas of attraction and avoidance, facilitating a detailed and nuanced analysis of crowd dynamics. Our approach systematically categorizes spatial zones based on density levels and evaluates the impact of attractors and repellers, providing valuable insights into potential congestion points and optimal crowd flow patterns. Visualization is achieved by overlaying quiver plots on heat maps, effectively highlighting spatial distributions and movement trends within the crowd. The proposed model has significant implications for urban planning, event management, and public safety, offering a robust tool for data-driven decision-making in crowd management. Preliminary assessments indicate its potential in predicting and mitigating crowd-related challenges, laying a solid foundation for future research and practical applications in the field.

articleTitle: Optimization of Charging Station Deployment Based on Travel Chain Charging Load Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The increasing demand for electric vehicles has led to concerns about charging infrastructure. This study proposes an optimization framework for deploying charging stations based on travel chain charging load prediction. First, the theory of travel chains is applied to characterize the behavior of electric vehicle (EV) users, which serves as the basis for the developed predictive model that assesses charging loads in terms of both location and time. This model is then evaluated through Monte Carlo simulations to determine charging demands. Subsequently, to reduce the overall societal costs, an optimization method is applied for the arrangement of charging stations, considering their types, quantities, and locations. The results of this study provide valuable insights into optimizing charging station deployment strategies that can help balance the benefits among multiple entities involved in EV charging infrastructure planning.

articleTitle: A Critical Analysis on Cybersecurity of Intemet-of-Things in System Integration and Architecture of Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The furious growth of smart city initiatives has resulted in various cybersecurity challenges that must be addressed. This literature review investigates recent research about cyber security in smart cities by discussing issues such as Internet of Things (IoT) vulnerabilities and proposing remedies like machine learning or risk-based analytics. These works also shed light on current trends, barriers, and emerging technologies related to this field. Moreover, these findings contribute towards building robust strategies for protecting urban infrastructures while enhancing their adaptability against increased digitization in cities worldwide and ensuring residents' well-being. The outcomes of this study propose some robust approaches for securing our cities; therefore, it recommends having more secure plans so as not only to safeguard but also to foster flexibility, among other things that may arise with growing numbers. Through this analysis, we can create better systems that are useful when dealing with different types at an advanced level, specifically for smart environments in towns or other urban areas.

articleTitle: Decentralized Scheduling Strategy for Multi-Energy Stations Aggregating Large-scale Flexible Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The growing adoption of distributed energy resources (DERs) has sparked greater research attention towards multi-energy cluster control stations. Although previous research highlights the substantial grid flexibility and economic advantages associated with multi-energy cluster control stations, there remains a notable gap in adequately addressing the integration of security constraints within multi-energy cluster control stations. This paper introduces a market-based control mechanism in market, aiming to effectively manage multi-energy cluster control stations in an economically viable manner while safeguarding the security of system operations. Given the dynamic behaviors of batteries and responsive demands, this study employs a model predictive control (MPC) technique to manage constraints across various time intervals and integrate predictions for both generation and consumption activities. To mitigate computational challenges and address concerns regarding individual privacy, we have devised an effective distributed algorithm tailored for solving the optimal power flow (OPF) problem. In simpler terms, we're adding extra factors to help us understand how different consumers who also produce power affect each other through the power grid. This helps us figure out prices for electricity in specific locations, considering factors like how much energy is being used, how congested the grid is, and any power loss along the way. We've tested this approach using a standard power system model, and our results show that it works effectively and efficiently.

articleTitle: Market Compensation Mechanism for Industrial Loads Participating in Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The industrial load has a great potential for suppressing wind power fluctuation because of its characteristics of large power consumption and strong power controllability. When the energy-intensive industrial load participate in the frequency regulation market, the existing compensation mechanism formulated according to the characteristics of the generation units is not suitable for evaluating the actual frequency regulation effect. In this paper, based on the analysis of power regulation characteristics of typical industrial loads, a power coupling characteristic model is established, and the influence of power regulation on production is analyzed and quantified. Then, based on the characteristics of industrial load power regulation and the current market mechanism, the market compensation mechanism of energy-intensive industrial load participating in power grid frequency regulation is proposed.

articleTitle: Analysis on Dynamic Characteristics of Corona Discharge in Low Concentration Methane-Air Mixture at Micro-Nano Scale
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: The detection of low concentration CH4 gas in underground coal mines is very important, and the micro-nano ionization sensor can quickly and accurately detect the composition and concentration of the gas. However, there is a lack of theoretical analysis of such sensors at the microscopic level. Based on the theory of fluid dynamics, a two-dimensional needle-plate discharge model is employed to simulate and study the dynamic discharge process of low concentration methane-air mixture at micro-nano scale. Based on the model, various characteristics during discharge period are analyzed, including the spatiotemporal evolution of electron density, the variation of electric field intensity and output current density. By changing the concentration of CH4 at atmospheric pressure, it can be concluded that the output current density of the ionization sensor decreases with the increase of CH4 concentration. Also, this research has a certain guiding significance for the preparation of micro-nano ionization methane sensor.

articleTitle: Risk Prediction and Assessment of High Voltage Transmission Lines under Typhoon Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Typhoon disasters frequently occur in East and Southeast Asia, posing a high risk of causing large-scale power outages in the power system. To investigate the impact of typhoon disasters on the high-voltage power grid, a risk assessment method combining model-driven and data-driven is proposed, which can predict the fault of power grid in advance and provide support for power grid operators to generate emergency dispatching plans. At the level of model-driven, the failure model of power equipment under typhoon disasters is established, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms of how typhoon wind speed affects transmission tower line system. At the level of data-driven, the collected meteorological data, power grid data and geographic information data are input into the SMOTE -LightGBM algorithm after data preprocessing and data augmentation, and then the probability of power grid failure can be predicted, preventing cascading power failures. Finally, the simulation uses the actual power system of a province of China and the data of typhoon ‘Doksuri’ to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, which can serve as a valuable reference for emergency warning, disaster prevention and mitigation in Asia.

articleTitle: Identification of Electrical Equipment Based on V-I Trajectory, Odd Harmonic Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 8th International Conference on Smart Grid and Smart Cities (ICSGSC)
abstract: Non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM) and identification are important to smart grid construction and safe operation. A method combining mixed feature matrix and convolutional neural network based on V-I trajectory and odd harmonic components is proposed and proved for non-intrusive electrical load monitoring technology. In the paper, the specific contents are to analyze the basic characteristics of electrical equipment, including steady-state and transient characteristics of input current. Six simulation circuits of single-phase AC power supply powered electrical equipment are established by means of MATLAB/Simulink using Electrical or Electronic blockset, including heater, hair dryers LED string, adapter, variable frequency air conditioner (air-CON), and variable frequency refrigerators, as the electrical equipment to be analyzed and identified. The grid side current waveforms and spectrums, V-I trajectories, and odd harmonic current components of these six load models are extracted as basic features. The mixed feature matrix using V-I trajectory and odd harmonic features, as well as convolutional neural network (CNN), are proposed for the analysis and identification of electrical equipment. After training and testing on the PLAID dataset, the system can effectively identify electrical equipment under steady-state operation. In addition, three different detection methods are compared and analyzed to verify the superiority of the proposed method for analyzing and identifying electrical equipment based on mixed feature matrix and convolutional neural network.

Author Keywords: Analysis and identification of electrical equipment
